question.problem: Evaluate the integral ${\int }_{C}\sqrt{x}y\,\text{d}s$, where the curve $C$ is given in polar form by $r=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
In polar coordinates, the formula for the line integral is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

 

The connection between polar and Cartesian coordinates gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta , \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

So, along our curve, we have $x=4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ and $y=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $, where $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.$

Now, if $f(x,y)=\sqrt{x}y$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot 4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =8|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta |\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =8{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta |=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ because $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}⟹\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \ge 0.$

Next, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta } & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  & =\sqrt{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\sqrt{x}y\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}8{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot 4\cdot \text{d}\theta  \\  & =32{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ $\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}32{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  & =32{\int }_{1}^{0}-{u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =32{\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =32\cdot \frac{1}{3}{u}^{3}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{32}{3}({1}^{3}-{0}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{32}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
